v37: Rounded icon tiles replace the old outlined text buttons. Hover for control names; right-click app tiles for actions. The ellipsis near running apps lists all windows. The ellipsis in the system cluster shows the original Windows tray for 25 seconds.

HUD TASKBAR - v36

The taskbar is a native desktop component, not part of the click-through wallpaper.
Each monitor gets its own JARVIS/SHIELD style and theme. It registers as an appbar
so maximized windows leave space for it. It hides for fullscreen apps. Explorer
keeps running.

START opens Windows Start. FIND opens Windows Search. VIEW opens Task View.
App buttons activate, restore or minimize windows; right-click for normal close
and pinning. APPS lists all running windows, including overflow and other screens.
Pinned shortcuts are imported from Windows when available. Right-click to unpin.

HUD opens the regular HudWall settings menu. SYS opens Windows quick settings
(volume/network/Bluetooth). ALERT and the clock open notifications/calendar.
DESK shows the desktop. These flyouts remain Windows components.

TRAY temporarily restores the original Windows taskbars for 25 seconds so all
existing notification-area icons remain accessible. They are not embedded into
the HUD bar. Say Jarvis show HUD taskbar to return immediately, or wait.

RECOVERY
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T restores Windows and disables replacement. You can also use
HUD > HUD taskbar > Restore Windows taskbar, or say Jarvis restore Windows taskbar.
Re-enable through the same menu or say Jarvis enable HUD taskbar.

A separate watchdog must be ready before the original taskbars are hidden. If
HudWall exits or crashes, Windows taskbars and their previous auto-hide state are
restored. A recovery record lives in %USERPROFILE%\.HudWall\taskbar-recovery.json.
Normal shutdown removes it; startup also recovers an interrupted prior session.

Pins/enabled state are saved in assets\taskbar.json. The organizer's stable
profile, fence contents and existing files are not moved or reset.

If the HUD is unresponsive, run Restore Windows Taskbar.cmd from the app folder.
It restores the native bars through a separate process and disables replacement.
